question: Why are Hollywood scripts still typed in a plain typewriter font with fixed margins?
answer: So that a page means a minute. In the standard layout, 12-point Courier with set margins, one page runs close to one minute of screen time. That turns the script into a measuring tool: assistant directors break scenes into eighths of a page and build the shooting schedule and budget from those counts.
